explanation: Hierarchical chunking searches precisely with child chunks and then replaces the results with broader parent chunks before passing them to the model, so it provides both precision and context. Making the chunks smaller reduces the context even further. Without chunking, the entire document becomes a single vector and search precision drops. Default chunking is a unit of about 300 tokens that respects sentence boundaries, so it has no effect of expanding context.

prompt: An AI service team will run a two-week load test on a specific Amazon Bedrock model before launching a new chatbot. Fixed throughput is needed only during this period, and the team wants to cancel immediately when the test ends. The usage plan after the test is undecided, so long-term commitments must be avoided. Considering cost, which configuration is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Purchase Provisioned Throughput with a 6-month commitment to receive the hourly discount.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Purchase Provisioned Throughput with a 1-month commitment and delete it right after two weeks.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use only batch inference jobs without reserving throughput, in place of the fixed throughput requirement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Purchase Provisioned Throughput with no commitment and delete it when the test ends.

explanation: If fixed throughput is needed, Provisioned Throughput is the answer, and the no-commitment option can be deleted at any time, so it meets the requirement to cancel after two weeks. Hourly charges continue until it is deleted, so do not forget to delete it. The 1-month and 6-month commitments cannot be deleted until the term ends, so they conflict with the constraint of avoiding long-term commitments. Batch inference does not reserve throughput, so it does not meet the fixed throughput requirement.

prompt: A marketing team wants to create product promotional images by entering only a text description, without a separate photo shoot. During the adoption review, a request came up that the whole team should understand how models such as Stable Diffusion work. Which statement BEST explains the basic principle by which a diffusion model generates images?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It predicts the next word as a probability based on the preceding words and context and attaches the words one after another.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It generates images by learning the process of adding noise and removing it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It finds the image closest to the input description in a repository and returns a copy of it as is.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It cuts an image into small pieces and then reassembles them in the original order to increase the resolution.

explanation: A diffusion model generates images by learning the process of adding noise and removing it. Predicting the next word as a probability and attaching the words in sequence is the approach of language models that generate text. Finding a stored image and copying it is search, not generating a new image. The explanation of reassembling pieces has nothing to do with the generation principle of a diffusion model.

prompt: A fintech company is choosing a candidate model for a generative AI app. Before deployment, it must check how often the candidate model produces responses containing stereotypes about occupations or gender, and there is no time for people to read each response. What is the MOST appropriate way to score the model responses with an evaluation prompt dataset?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Estimate response bias by aggregating the number of InvokeModel calls with AWS CloudTrail.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Register occupation and gender in the Guardrails denied topics as a substitute for evaluation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Score the responses with a judge model and a stereotyping metric in an Amazon Bedrock evaluation job.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Scan Amazon S3 for sensitive information with Amazon Macie and use the results as a bias metric.

explanation: The judge model method in Amazon Bedrock evaluations has a built-in metric that scores whether a response contains stereotypes, so candidate models can be compared before deployment using an evaluation dataset. AWS CloudTrail leaves only a record of invocations and does not score response content. Guardrails denied topics is a feature that blocks specific topics at runtime, not an evaluation that measures a model's bias. Amazon Macie is a service that finds sensitive data in Amazon S3, so it has nothing to do with stereotypes in responses.

prompt: An online bookstore wants to put personalized recommended book lists in its app based on users' purchase and click history. The history data is already accumulated in Amazon S3, but the company has no staff to build a recommendation algorithm itself and the launch schedule is tight. It needs the method with the LEAST operational overhead. What should it choose?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Implement a collaborative filtering algorithm from scratch in Amazon SageMaker and host it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Analyze review sentiment with Amazon Comprehend and show the highest-scoring books to everyone.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Build an Amazon Lex chatbot that asks users directly about their preferred genres.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Upload the interaction data to Amazon Personalize and build a recommendation model.

explanation: The managed service that creates personalized recommendations from interaction data between users and items is Amazon Personalize, and you do not have to build the algorithm yourself. Implementing it directly in Amazon SageMaker is possible, but it has the largest development and operational burden. Showing the same books to everyone based on review sentiment scores is not personalization. Asking genres through a chatbot is not recommendation based on history.

prompt: Internal HR policy documents are revised every week, and answers to employee questions must cite the source documents. The documents are in Amazon S3, and the HR team wants revisions to be reflected immediately. The development team has only two people, so it wants to reflect the latest content without retraining the model. Which approach has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fine-tune the model with the policy documents every time they are revised, purchase new Provisioned Throughput, and delete the previous model.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Paste the entire policy text as is into the prompt of every request and pass it to the model.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Register policy clauses in the guardrail word filter so that those clauses appear in responses.

choices.label: D
choices.text: RAG that ingests and embeds the Amazon S3 documents with an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base and passes the search results to the model

explanation: The documents change frequently and source citation is needed, so RAG using a knowledge base is appropriate. The documents are split into chunks and embedded into a vector index, the chunks closest to the question are passed to the model, and no retraining is needed. Fine-tuning has to be repeated with every revision, so its cost and operations are large. Putting the entire policy in the prompt causes length limit and cost problems. The word filter is for blocking and is not a feature for providing knowledge.

prompt: A fintech company is comparing two binary classification models. The classification threshold for production is still being discussed with the business team and has not been decided. The company therefore wants to first see how well the models distinguish positives from negatives regardless of the threshold. Which metric is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: AUC: a value that represents the ability to give higher scores to positive examples regardless of the threshold

choices.label: B
choices.text: Compare only a single value, the overall accuracy calculated assuming a threshold of 0.5, between the two models.

choices.label: C
choices.text: RMSE: looks at the average size of the error between predictions and actual values in continuous value prediction

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use only the recall calculated at one specific threshold as the model selection criterion.

explanation: AUC does not depend on the score threshold and measures the ability to give positives higher scores than negatives, so it is suitable for a comparison where the threshold is undecided. A value near 0.5 is at the level of random guessing, and the closer to 1, the better. The accuracy at a threshold of 0.5 or the recall at a specific threshold changes when the threshold changes. RMSE is a metric for regression models.

prompt: A customer service chatbot keeps writing unnecessary sentences even after it finishes its answer, so response time is long and token costs are rising. The prompt has been set to make the chatbot output a delimiter string "### END" at the end of the answer. The company wants generation to stop the moment this string is output, to reduce unnecessary token generation. Which inference setting is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lower the temperature value close to 0 to reduce the randomness of the output so that the answer comes out in the same form every time.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set the Top K value to 1 to limit the next-token candidates to one.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Specify the string "### END" in the stop sequences so that generation stops when that string is generated.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fix the response length (max tokens) at the minimum allowed value to cut the response short.

explanation: If you specify a delimiter string in the stop sequences, the model stops producing tokens after it generates that string, so it meets the requirement to stop immediately at a specific string. Lowering the temperature only reduces randomness and does not stop at a specific string. Setting Top K to 1 only reduces the number of candidates, and the stopping point stays the same. Fixing the response length at the minimum would cut the answer off midway regardless of the delimiter string, which breaks normal answers.

prompt: In an advertising company's slogan generation app, feedback said that the results were too scattered, so the Top P value was lowered from 0.9 to 0.5. The person in charge must explain to the team how this change affects the responses. In terms of the candidate pool from which the model selects the next token, which statement describes the effect of this change MOST accurately?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The top 50% of cumulative probability is added, so the candidate range widens and low-probability tokens are selected often.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The number of next-token candidates is fixed at exactly 50, so the size of the candidate pool becomes the same.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only candidates within the top 50% of cumulative probability are considered, so the candidate range narrows and diversity decreases.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The maximum length of generated responses is cut in half, so only shorter slogans are produced.

explanation: Top P is a value that cuts off candidates based on cumulative probability, so lowering it leaves only the most likely candidates, which makes responses more conservative and reduces diversity. The explanation that the candidate range widens has the direction reversed. Fixing the candidates to a set number is the behavior of Top K, and with Top P the number of candidates differs for each token. The response length is determined by a separate length parameter.

prompt: A credit card company is evaluating a credit card fraud detection model. The loss from missing an actual fraudulent transaction is much greater than the cost of suspecting a legitimate transaction and sending the customer a confirmation text message. Fraud is only a tiny fraction of all transactions. Which metric should be checked FIRST for this requirement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Precision: the ratio of transactions predicted as fraud by the model that were actually fraud

choices.label: B
choices.text: Recall: the ratio of actual fraudulent transactions that the model found as fraud

choices.label: C
choices.text: Accuracy: the ratio of correctly classified transactions among all transactions

choices.label: D
choices.text: RMSE: a value obtained by squaring the difference between predicted and actual values, averaging, and taking the square root

explanation: The goal is to reduce missed fraud, so recall, the ratio of actual positives that were found, should be the priority. Precision is the ratio of correct predictions among those predicted as fraud, so it is a metric for reducing false positives, and in this situation the cost of false positives is small. Accuracy is inappropriate because with imbalanced data in which fraud is a tiny minority, it comes out high even if everything is predicted as legitimate. RMSE is an error metric for regression models, so it is not used for classification problems.

domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
prompt: At an internal security review meeting, the security manager of a company that plans to launch an Amazon Bedrock-based chatbot asks who is responsible for preventing prompt injection. The chatbot is a web application that receives customer questions and passes them to the model. Under the shared responsibility model, which statement is MOST accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: AWS automatically sanitizes all inputs, so customers do not need to implement input validation separately.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The customer must directly inspect and manage the physical security of the data centers and the model hosting hardware.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The model provider is solely responsible for injection defense, so the customer application takes no action.

choices.label: D
choices.text: AWS protects the infrastructure that underlies the service, and the customer is responsible for application-level security such as preventing prompt injection.

explanation: AWS documentation explains that AWS is responsible for the security of the physical data centers, the network, and the Amazon Bedrock service itself, while the customer is responsible for preventing application-level vulnerabilities such as prompt injection. The statement that input validation is unnecessary is the opposite of the documentation's recommendation. Physical security and hardware are AWS's area of responsibility. The statement that the model provider is solely responsible for injection defense does not exist in the shared responsibility model.
